title: The AI revolution
intro: From the American century to the AI revolution: how the advantage in computing moved from a nation to a laboratory, to the engineers who left it, to a chip designer, and to the labs that scaled a published idea.
end: The advantage kept moving: from a nation that made half the world's industrial output, to a monopoly's laboratory, to eight engineers who walked out, to a foundry that made chips for everyone, to the designer whose chips the field ran on, to the labs that scaled a paper Google gave away. Explore any year with the panel, or play the age of revolutions.

steps.title: The American century
steps.text: After the Second World War the United States made half of the world's industrial output and held 80% of its gold. At Bretton Woods it made the system rest on gold and the dollar, and under the Marshall Plan it sent $13.3 billion to 17 European countries. In 1950 its GDP was 1,456 billion 1990 dollars; the Soviet Union's was 510.

steps.title: The transistor
steps.text: In 1947 John Bardeen, Walter Brattain and William Shockley of Bell Labs invented the transistor. The laboratory belonged to the Bell System: AT&T, 24 local companies and Western Electric. The three shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics; work done at Bell Labs has won eleven Nobel Prizes. Its advantage, as the research records it: technology, and the Bell System's capital.

steps.title: The traitorous eight
steps.text: In 1955 Shockley founded his own laboratory. Eight of its engineers, Robert Noyce and Gordon Moore among them, left and founded Fairchild Semiconductor on 18 September 1957 with Sherman Fairchild's backing, to make transistors of silicon when germanium was still the common material. Its alumni went on to create dozens of companies, Intel and AMD among them.

steps.title: The integrated circuit
steps.text: In 1958 Jack Kilby made the first integrated circuit at Texas Instruments. In 1959 Fairchild developed the planar process, and Robert Noyce invented the monolithic integrated circuit. Fairchild sold its first 100 devices to IBM at $150 each, for the B-70 bomber's computer. Kilby won the Nobel Prize in 2000.

steps.title: The microprocessor
steps.text: Noyce and Moore founded Intel in 1968, and Federico Faggin left Fairchild for Intel in 1970. In 1971 Intel introduced the 4004, built for Busicom: 2,300 transistors on one chip, made possible by the silicon-gate process. In 1975 Moore revised his forecast to a doubling of components every two years.

steps.title: The PC and the x86
steps.text: Intel made the first commercial microprocessor, but the PC made it Intel's primary business. The IBM PC, released on 12 August 1981, used an Intel 8088. In 1983 Japanese memory makers squeezed Intel's profits and Andy Grove refocused it on microprocessors. In 1986 Compaq, the first IBM PC clone maker, shipped the first 80386 system, beating IBM and making Intel a key component supplier. At the end of 1999 Intel was worth $274.43 billion.

steps.title: The foundry
steps.text: In 1987 Taiwan's government, its research institute ITRI and private investors founded TSMC, the world's first dedicated foundry, with Morris Chang at its head. Philips put up $58 million and its production technology for 27.6% of it. In the second quarter of 2026 TSMC took 72.5% of the revenue of the ten largest foundries.

steps.title: The GPU
steps.text: In 1996 Jensen Huang cut Nvidia from 100 people to 40 to focus on one chip. Nvidia went public on 22 January 1999, and late that year released the GeForce 256, the first product it called a GPU: 17 million transistors, made by TSMC. At the end of 1999 Nvidia was worth $0.96 billion, Intel $274.43 billion. In December 2000 Nvidia agreed to buy 3dfx's intellectual assets.

steps.title: CUDA
steps.text: CUDA, Nvidia's development environment, was created in 2004 and released in 2007. Twenty years on it has 6 million developers, and it dominates the market for GPU development against AMD's ROCm.

steps.title: AlexNet
steps.text: In 2012 Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever and Geoffrey Hinton trained AlexNet, 60 million parameters, for five to six days on two Nvidia GTX 580s, $500 each. It won ImageNet with a top-5 error of 15.3%, more than 10.8 points ahead. At the end of 2012 Nvidia was worth $7.66 billion, Intel $101.94 billion and TSMC $86.83 billion; at the end of 2017 Nvidia was worth $117.26 billion.

steps.title: Attention Is All You Need
steps.text: On 12 June 2017 eight Google researchers posted the Transformer, built on attention alone. Earlier models with recurrence were hard to spread across GPUs; the Transformer reached 41.8 BLEU after 3.5 days on eight GPUs. Google published it, all eight authors later left, and the paper has been cited more than 150,000 times.

steps.title: Scaling
steps.text: GPT-1 had 117 million parameters; the full GPT-2, in November 2019, 1.5 billion. In January 2020 Kaplan and colleagues found that loss falls as a power law in model size, data and compute. GPT-3, in May 2020, had 175 billion, ten times any earlier dense model. Microsoft had invested $1 billion in 2019, and licensed GPT-3 exclusively in September 2020.

steps.title: ChatGPT
steps.text: ChatGPT was released on 30 November 2022 and had 100 million monthly users two months later. In January 2023 Microsoft invested another $10 billion, much of it for Azure compute. By February 2026 ChatGPT had 900 million weekly users. OpenAI was valued at $500 billion in October 2025, and later at $852 billion.

steps.title: A test of the walls
steps.text: DeepSeek-V3 needed only 2.788 million H800 GPU hours to train, by its authors' account. On 27 January 2025 Nvidia lost more than $589 billion of market value, which Forbes called the biggest single-day loss for any company. On 29 October 2025 it became the first company worth $5 trillion.
steps.reading: A wall is tested when a rival finds a way around it.

steps.title: Five trillion dollars
steps.text: In 2023 Nvidia became the seventh US company worth $1 trillion, and went from $1 trillion to $2 trillion in 180 days; Apple and Microsoft each took over 500. On 29 October 2025 it became the first company worth $5 trillion. Its share of AI accelerators is expected to be about 75% in 2026, down from a peak near 87% in 2024. Its advantage, as the research records it: technology, supply, patents, capital, talent and scale.

steps.title: The present
steps.text: Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft and SpaceX are forecast to spend $803 to $828 billion on capital in 2026. Over eight quarters Nvidia's data-centre revenue has equalled 39% to 47% of what the largest clouds spend. Anthropic was valued at $965 billion in May 2026, OpenAI at $852 billion.
